events.sourceNotes: O03 supplies both complete alternatives. P06’s left body is overlapped; visible fragments are compatible. The face does not explicitly define a counter-counter chain or how reaction windows reopen.

recommendedPolicies: One actual own physical card; preserve its ID/weather/metadata outside draw/discard circulation until the whole event and nested effects complete, unless a legitimate Synchronize claim transfers it.

Capture ordered live target trainers and original active instances at event use; exclude spectators/eliminated seats. Moltres excludes actor; Zapdos includes actor LAST, starting with the actor’s next live trainer. Do not silently reuse Mew Blessing’s self-first order.
No printed distance clause for Moltres or Zapdos; reach all explicitly scoped actives. Do not target reserves or infer a Pokémon move/command-target window.

Conservative Moltres response policy distinguishes 打出 from 使用: use one actual own kind:command card as the Take this! response, or pass. It is not using the card to perform a Pokémon move, so no Power/Burn/Paralysis sunny-command restriction/command-user lock/move limit/Moxie/Pressure/Cute Charm is invoked. No printed virtual-command conversion for this response is established.
Moltres response prompt is public independent of holdings; show eligible actual response cards only to the current target trainer. Optional expiry can pass under existing digital timer policy.

Zapdos opens no printed Dodge/command-response window. Judge separately for each target trainer; use Drought’s final judgment. An empty supply creates no result and no damage, including no fabricated thunderstorm. The card’s own thunderstorm weather is not its judgment result.

Zapdos damage should use the still-original target’s current level at damage resolution, after its final judgment. This timing is a bounded implementation interpretation; the face says damage equals that Pokémon’s level without a separate snapshot rule.

Represent Moltres and Zapdos as external named damage sources with no player owner. Do not substitute event user’s active, source modifiers, retaliation recipient or defeat reward. Receiving immunity/Defense/Dratini/Shed Skin/Water Absorb/Battle Armor/Oblivious/Synchronize, rescue and immediate victory remain shared rules.

A target defeated/replaced during nested processing must not transfer its saved event slot to an incoming reserve. Defense cleanup belongs to whole-card end; Synchronize can claim the actual event card once while later targets continue.
Early Bird names only Jigglypuff and Mr. Mime, giving no protection from Moltres, Zapdos or Articuno. Gas affects actual Pokémon traits, not printed event effects.

Articuno is source-reviewed but not enabled by this record. Its first branch cancels only the one target’s event effect, not a whole global event; second branch follows actual status application, not ordinary Play or a prevented/failed status attempt.

A coherent Articuno implementation needs generic before-event-target and after-final-status-applied hooks across existing events/status sources, actual-card payment, privacy-safe response queues, restart/clock/vote state, and a documented counter-chain/reopen policy. Sources do not explicitly settle counter-counter behavior; implementation policy must remain distinguished from printed text.

Accepted booklet current-turn-first counterclockwise order provides a basis for ordering simultaneous trainers’ reaction opportunities, but a reaction queue and automatic pass policy are digital implementation choices.

Do not call Articuno unreadable or ask for its supplied face again; remaining work is shared response machinery and explicit bounded policy. No deck quantities or weather-copy distribution follow from these displayed samples.
